title: Minimum XOR Sum of Two Arrays
summary: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, rearrange the elements of nums2 to minimize the XOR sum of the two arrays.
statement: Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2 of equal length, rearrange the elements of nums2 to minimize the XOR sum of the two arrays. The XOR sum is calculated by performing the XOR operation on corresponding elements of both arrays and summing the results. For example, the XOR sum of [1,2,3] and [3,2,1] is (1 XOR 3) + (2 XOR 2) + (3 XOR 1) = 2 + 0 + 2 = 4. Return the minimized XOR sum after rearrangement.
constraints: The arrays have equal length from 1 through 14.
Rearrange nums2 to minimize the sum of XORs at corresponding positions.
hints: A bitmask can record exactly which values from nums2 have already been assigned.
The mask's set-bit count identifies the next nums1 position.
Try every unused partner and relax the cost of the mask with that bit added.
Every complete mask path represents one permutation, and dynamic programming retains the cheapest prefix for each equivalent set of remaining choices.
editorial: Every complete mask path represents one permutation, and dynamic programming retains the cheapest prefix for each equivalent set of remaining choices.

tests.explanation: Pairing one with three and two with two gives XOR cost two.
The minimum over all one-to-one assignments is eight.
